Question: Assume: 1) no-inter player trading occurs, 2) there are no development cards left to draw, 3) in-hand VP cards count as points, 4) can use the combined Trade/Build phase, 5)For maritime trade, a city on a special harbor grants a 1:1 trade rate for its resource, while a city on a generic harbor grants a 3:2 trade rate for any resource, 6) There is no limit on the number of settlements the red player has.  What is the maximum number of settlements that the red player can have by the end of the turn, given the player rolls a 6 in this turn? Return the answer in the following format: [prev: <number of settlements before the turn>, new: <number of settlements after the turn>].
Rationale: According to the given board stateIn the question, The red player has three settlements. The red player currently has the following resource cards: [bricks: 3, wool: 4, grains: 4, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. Since the player rolls is 6, the player would get 1 brick resource card. This would result in the player having [brick: 4, wool: 4, grain: 4, lumber: 3, ore: 3]. According to the rules, the red player has enough resources and positions to build 2 more settlements (paying 1 brick, 1 lumber, 1 wool, 1 grain for each): (9, 8, 10) and at the corner of 8 forest hex. This way the player has 2 more settlements added. Now with the remaining resources, use 1 brick and 1 lumber to build one road between (8, 4) and build another settlement (paying 1 brick, 1 lumber, 1 wool, 1 grain) near the special harbor. This way the player can get a total of 3 more settlements by the end of this turn.
